title: Practice Set 7 — Joins: Combining DataFrames
description: Apply every join type to NordGrid's data: inner joins with row-loss awareness, left joins to preserve readings, anti joins to find missing meters, column ambiguity resolution, and a multi-hop enrichment pipeline.

datasets.description: NordGrid meter readings. 120 rows. Meter IDs M-0001 through M-0120. Meters M-0101 to M-0120 have no match in the meters reference table.
NordGrid meter reference table. 110 rows. Meter IDs M-0001 to M-0100 (matched) plus M-0121 to M-0130 (unreported). Has a 'region' column that overlaps with the readings table (ambiguity source).

columns.name: region
columns.description: Same column name as readings — creates ambiguity on join

datasets.description: NordGrid substation reference table. 8 rows. Linked to meters via substation_id.

tasks.title: Enrich NordGrid Readings with Meter Metadata

description.context: NordGrid's Silver pipeline needs to enrich daily meter readings with customer_type and substation_id from the meter reference table. The readings table has 120 meters, but the reference table only has metadata for 100 of them. The remaining 20 meters were recently installed and their metadata has not yet been entered.
description.task: Read both CSV files (header=True, inferSchema=True). Join the readings with the meters reference table on meter_id using an inner join. Store the result in a variable called enriched. Then count how many readings were lost due to missing metadata and store that number in rows_lost.
description.validationHint: The inner join silently drops readings where meter_id has no match in the reference table. Your enriched DataFrame should have 100 rows, not 120. The 20 recently installed meters are excluded.

tasks.partialCredit: 4 independent assertions. Each passed assertion earns 1/4 credit.

fields.label: An inner join of 120 readings against 100 meters returns 100 rows. What happened to the other 20?
options: Inner join silently drops readings whose meter_id has no match in the reference table — the 20 newly installed meters are excluded
Spark caches them in a side table you can recover with df.dropped() — they're temporarily quarantined
Inner join keeps every left-side row; the missing 20 must be a CSV parse failure earlier in the pipeline
fields.correctAnswer: Inner join silently drops readings whose meter_id has no match in the reference table — the 20 newly installed meters are excluded
fields.rationale: Inner join only keeps rows present on BOTH sides — unmatched readings vanish without warning. Spark has no .dropped() method.

tasks.title: Preserve All Readings with a Left Join

description.context: The inner join from the previous scenario dropped 20 readings from recently installed meters. NordGrid's data quality team requires that no readings are ever silently lost — all 120 readings must appear in the Silver output, even if metadata is not yet available. The team will flag missing-metadata readings for follow-up rather than discarding them.
description.task: Join readings with the meters reference table using a left join on meter_id to preserve all readings. For the 20 meters without metadata, the customer_type and substation_id columns will be null. After the join, both tables have a 'region' column — resolve the ambiguity by dropping the meters table's region column. Store the result in a variable called all_readings. Also count how many readings have null customer_type and store in missing_metadata_count.
description.validationHint: A left join preserves all 120 readings. 20 readings will have null customer_type. The region ambiguity must be resolved or subsequent operations will fail.

tasks.partialCredit: 5 independent assertions. Each passed assertion earns 1/5 credit.

fields.label: After df.join(meters, 'meter_id', 'left'), both tables had a 'region' column. What's the safest fix?
options: Drop the meters-side region before the join: df.join(meters.drop('region'), 'meter_id', 'left')
Use df.join(meters, ['meter_id','region'], 'left') — joining on region too removes the duplicate column
Cast both region columns to the same type — the duplicate disappears once they match
fields.correctAnswer: Drop the meters-side region before the join: df.join(meters.drop('region'), 'meter_id', 'left')
fields.rationale: Joining on region would drop readings whose region disagrees with the reference (silent data loss).Casting doesn't deduplicate columns.

tasks.title: Predict Row Counts for Different Join Types

description.context: Each join type selects a different region of the Venn diagram between two tables. INNER keeps only the OVERLAP. LEFT keeps everything from the left side, padding right-side columns with null where no match exists. RIGHT mirrors LEFT. FULL OUTER keeps everything from both sides. SEMI is a FILTERING join — it keeps left-side ROWS where a match exists in the right side, and returns ONLY the LEFT-SIDE COLUMNS (no enrichment). ANTI is the inverse of semi — it keeps left-side rows where NO match exists, again with only left-side columns. Semi and anti are filtering tools, not enrichment tools.
description.task: Predict the row count for each join type and recognize what semi returns.
description.validationHint: Draw a Venn diagram: 100 in the overlap, 20 readings-only, 10 meters-only. Each join type selects a different part of this diagram.

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content: readings: 120 rows, meter_ids M-0001 to M-0120. meters: 110 rows, meter_ids M-0001 to M-0100 plus M-0121 to M-0130. Overlap: 100. Readings-only: 20 (M-0101 to M-0120). Meters-only: 10 (M-0121 to M-0130). No duplicate keys in either side.

fields.label: Inner join (how='inner'): how many rows?
fields.rationale: Inner keeps only the 100 matching meter IDs. 20 readings-only and 10 meters-only are both dropped.

fields.label: Left join (how='left'): how many rows?
fields.rationale: Left preserves all 120 readings.The 100 matched rows get metadata.The 20 unmatched readings get nulls for metadata columns.

fields.label: Full outer join (how='full'): how many rows?
fields.rationale: Full outer keeps everything: 100 matched + 20 readings-only + 10 meters-only = 130.

fields.label: Anti join — readings NOT in meters (how='anti'): how many rows?
fields.rationale: Anti join keeps readings whose meter_id has NO match in meters. M-0101 to M-0120 = 20 readings.

fields.label: A semi join of readings against meters (how='semi') returns how many columns?
options: All 7 combined columns from both tables — semi join is just an inner join with deduplication of the join key.
Only the 4 readings columns — semi join is a FILTER that uses the right table to decide which left rows to keep but does not add right-side columns.
Only the 4 meters columns — semi join keeps the right table's columns because the right table is the 'authority' for membership.
Only the 1 join key column (meter_id) — semi join projects to the join key only as a metadata operation.
fields.correctAnswer: Only the 4 readings columns — semi join is a FILTER that uses the right table to decide which left rows to keep but does not add right-side columns.
fields.rationale: Semi and anti are FILTERING joins, not enrichment joins.They check membership in the right table and emit ONLY left-side columns.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Semi does not enrich; the right table is consulted but not projected.

tasks.title: Find NordGrid's Unreported Meters

description.context: NordGrid's operations team needs to find meters that are registered in the reference table but did not submit readings this period. These unreported meters may indicate communication failures or decommissioned equipment that was not removed from the reference list. The team wants a list of meter IDs and their customer types — they do not want any reading columns added to the output.
description.task: Use an anti join to find meters in the meters reference table that have no corresponding reading in the readings table. Store the result in a variable called unreported. The result should contain only columns from the meters reference table.
description.validationHint: The anti join uses the meters table as the left side and readings as the right side. 10 meters (M-0121 to M-0130) have no readings. The result should have 10 rows with meters-table columns only.

tasks.partialCredit: 4 independent assertions. Each passed assertion earns 1/4 credit.

fields.label: How do you find meters in the reference table that have NO reading in the readings table?
options: meters.join(readings, 'meter_id', 'left_anti') — anti join keeps left rows that have no right match
meters.join(readings, 'meter_id', 'left').filter(col('daily_kw').isNull()) — left join + null filter
readings.join(meters, 'meter_id', 'right_anti') — right anti from the readings side
fields.correctAnswer: meters.join(readings, 'meter_id', 'left_anti') — anti join keeps left rows that have no right match
fields.rationale: left_anti is the canonical 'in A but not in B' operator and returns only left-side columns.

description.context: Four join rules drive most production bugs. (1) on='meter_id' merges only the JOIN KEY column. Other columns sharing names (like 'region') are NOT merged — they appear TWICE in the result, creating ambiguity that breaks subsequent col('region') references. (2) Spark's optimizer picks BROADCAST JOIN automatically when one side is below spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10 MB). The small side is shipped to every executor, eliminating the shuffle. For larger sides, Spark uses SORT-MERGE or HASH JOIN. (3) Use SEMI for filtering by membership, ANTI for filtering by non-membership; never use inner/left when you only need the left side's rows. (4) Left join row count = LEFT side count when right has unique keys; if right has DUPLICATE join keys, the left rows are multiplied, which is a common silent bug.
description.task: Identify the correct behavior or strategy for each scenario.
description.validationHint: Think about what happens to the column list after each join type, and when Spark broadcasts vs shuffles.

evidence.title: Input sample
evidence.content: Four scenarios from a production code review.

fields.label: Both readings and meters have a 'region' column. After df_readings.join(df_meters, on='meter_id', how='inner'), how many 'region' columns exist in the result?
options: One — the string form on='meter_id' merges ALL shared column names automatically, including 'region'. Spark's column resolver deduplicates by name during the analysis pass, so the result schema always contains a single entry per logical column.

Two — on='meter_id' merges ONLY the join key. Other shared column names ('region') remain duplicated, producing two columns named 'region' in the result and causing ambiguity errors on subsequent col('region') references.

Zero — Spark detects the ambiguity and drops both 'region' columns to avoid runtime errors. The Catalyst optimizer treats unresolved joins as a safety hazard and rewrites them to drop the conflicting columns before execution.

One — Spark always keeps only the LEFT table's version of any duplicate column name. The right-side duplicate is silently dropped because the left input's schema takes priority during the join's column-resolution phase.
fields.correctAnswer: Two — on='meter_id' merges ONLY the join key. Other shared column names ('region') remain duplicated, producing two columns named 'region' in the result and causing ambiguity errors on subsequent col('region') references.
fields.rationale: The 'on' argument controls only the join CONDITION; it deduplicates only the join key.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Only the join key is merged.
Option C: Spark does not auto-drop; it raises errors at use time.

fields.label: NordGrid joins 120 rows of readings (120 MB) with 8 rows of substations (1 KB). Which join strategy does Spark use?
options: Shuffle hash join — both sides are hashed and shuffled by the join key, with one side built into a hash table per partition.
Broadcast hash join — the 1 KB substations table is below the autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10 MB), so Spark ships it to every executor and joins without shuffling readings.
Sort-merge join — both sides are sorted by the join key on every partition before being merged together.
Nested loop join — every reading row is compared against every substation row in a Cartesian fashion.
fields.correctAnswer: Broadcast hash join — the 1 KB substations table is below the autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10 MB), so Spark ships it to every executor and joins without shuffling readings.
fields.rationale: Broadcast joins are Spark's optimization for joining a large table with a small one: the small side is replicated to every executor, eliminating the.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Shuffle joins are used when both sides are too large to broadcast.

fields.label: An engineer wants to filter readings to only those from active meters. The active meter list is a separate DataFrame. Which join type should they use?
options: Inner join — it correctly filters and adds active-meter columns for completeness.
Left join — it preserves all readings and lets downstream code filter by null.
Semi join — it FILTERS readings by membership in the active list without adding any columns from that list; this is the dedicated tool for membership-based filtering.
Anti join — it returns readings NOT in the active list, which is the inverse of what is needed.
fields.correctAnswer: Semi join — it FILTERS readings by membership in the active list without adding any columns from that list; this is the dedicated tool for membership-based filtering.
fields.rationale: Semi join is the membership-test tool: keep left rows that have a match, return only left columns.
fields.distractorRationale:
Option A: Inner adds right-side columns the engineer does not want.
Option B: Left does not filter; it preserves all left rows.

fields.label: After a left join, the engineer finds 120 rows but expected only 100. What is the most likely cause?
options: The left join added 20 extra rows from the right table; left joins always include right-only rows when the optimizer chooses an outer plan.

The left join preserved 20 LEFT rows that have no match in the right; left always keeps every left row, so unmatched left rows show up with null right-side columns. The engineer expected an INNER join behavior.
The right table has 20 duplicate join keys, multiplying matched left rows by 2 each.
The join condition produced a partial Cartesian product because one side was missing a key column.
fields.correctAnswer: The left join preserved 20 LEFT rows that have no match in the right; left always keeps every left row, so unmatched left rows show up with null right-side columns. The engineer expected an INNER join behavior.
fields.rationale: LEFT preserves every left row by definition.If you got 120 rows but expected 100, you have 20 unmatched left rows with null right-columns.
fields.distractorRationale: Option A: Left does not include right-only rows; that is full outer.

tasks.title: Build NordGrid's Two-Hop Enrichment Pipeline

description.context: NordGrid's Silver enrichment pipeline must join three tables: readings → meters → substations. Readings connect to meters via meter_id. Meters connect to substations via substation_id. The final output must include the reading data, customer_type from meters, and substation_name from substations. All readings must be preserved (use left joins). Both the readings and meters tables have a 'region' column that creates ambiguity after the first join.
description.task: Write a pipeline that: (1) reads all three CSVs; (2) left-joins readings with meters on meter_id; (3) resolves the region ambiguity by dropping the meters table's region column; (4) left-joins the result with substations on substation_id; (5) selects the final columns: meter_id, daily_kw, date, region, customer_type, substation_name; (6) stores the result in a variable called enriched.
description.validationHint: All 120 readings must be preserved. 20 readings will have null customer_type and null substation_name (no meter metadata → no substation link). The final output has 6 columns.

tasks.partialCredit: 7 independent assertions. Each passed assertion earns 1/7 credit.

conceptsCombined: Left join to preserve all readings (Lesson 3)
Two-hop join chain: readings → meters → substations (Lesson 9)
Column ambiguity resolution for shared 'region' column (Lesson 7)
Null propagation through join chain — null substation_id from first join → null substation_name from second join (Lesson 3)
synthesisNotes.rationale: This is NordGrid's production enrichment pattern: chain two left joins through intermediate reference tables, handle ambiguity, and produce a clean.

fields.label: Three-table chain: readings → meters → substations, all left joins. What must happen between the two joins?
options: After the first join, drop the meters-side region (and any other duplicated key column) BEFORE joining substations, otherwise the second join hits ambiguous columns

Cache the intermediate DataFrame so the second join can re-use it without recomputing — Spark requires materialization between joins so the second join's Catalyst planner can read the intermediate's column statistics directly from the cached block manager.

Repartition by substation_id so the second join becomes a co-located shuffle — co-location eliminates the second join's network transfer and is the only way to chain three left joins without intermediate-stage failures.
fields.correctAnswer: After the first join, drop the meters-side region (and any other duplicated key column) BEFORE joining substations, otherwise the second join hits ambiguous columns
fields.rationale: Column ambiguity is a runtime error, not a perf issue.

selfCheck.foundationModuleException: Not applicable — Module 7 is Essential Operations phase.
selfCheck.theoryPracticeBoundary: Theory examples join readings with meters on meter_id using standard NordGrid data. Practice tasks use the same join pattern but with intentionally designed mismatches: 20 readings with no metadata and 10 meters with no readings. These mismatches force students to see the practical consequences of each join type rather than joining clean, fully-matched data. Task 4 reverses the join direction (meters anti-joined against readings) compared to the theory's example (readings anti-joined against active fleet).
selfCheck.crossModuleNotes: Task 2 requires resolving column ambiguity with drop() (Module 4 skill). Task 6 uses select() for the output schema contract (Module 4) and null handling awareness (Module 4, Lesson 6). The Essential Operations phase expects these cross-module combinations per §2.4.
selfCheck.datasetNotes: Three related tables with intentional key mismatches. Readings (120 rows) and meters (110 rows) share 100 meter IDs, with 20 readings-only and 10 meters-only. Both have a 'region' column to force ambiguity handling. Substations (8 rows) link through meters.substation_id for the two-hop join.
